items.title: Kenny Davern interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 16, 2001 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: Steve said 'Django Reinhardt.' So there you have it. ... you go back and catch the person or several persons that that person has heard.

ctx.x: I guess you know you look at the jazz scene today and there’s some things that are really positive. It’s been elevated to a real art form. But I wonder—

Who wants it? Where do people with originality — I mean there are some good ones out there. There’s Chris Potter, there’s Joe Lovano, there’s Billy Charlap. I mean they all know their deficiencies incidentally. At least Billy has admitted — like I say I play “Sunny Side of the Street.” I’ve heard at least 25, 30, 40, 50 versions of that tune by different people.” He says, “Yes,” he says, “I know,” he says, “I haven’t heard really anybody’s version of it.” To me it’s C, E7, bah-bah-bah. See? Now that’s what’s…
Now see, I thought I wasn’t going ask about it but—
